strategy.summary: Reproduce the order-dependence and singular-covariance bug in statsmodels linear_rainbow(use_distance=True) by building the buggy commit c14824302280 from source and running the PR's new tests in test_diagnostic.py. On the buggy revision the order-invariance, discrete-lattice, manual-ordering and center-deprecation tests should fail; on the fixed revision they should pass. Versions are unbounded per the context, so the plan uses current numpy/pandas/scipy from pip, with the buggy source built in place rather than taken from a nightly wheel.

system_packages: C and C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) for building statsmodels Cython extensions
build_commands: python -m pip install numpy scipy pandas patsy packaging cython pytest

strategy.reproducing_test: test_rainbow_use_distance_order_invariant (parametrized add_const False/True), test_rainbow_use_distance_order_invariant_discrete, test_rainbow_use_distance_matches_manual_ordering, test_rainbow_center_deprecated, in statsmodels/stats/tests/test_diagnostic.py; apply the PR test diff to the buggy checkout so these tests exist there, and remove test_rainbow_smoke_centered as the diff does
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy c14824302280 with the PR tests applied, the order-invariance tests fail (AssertionError from assert_allclose with default rtol 1e-7 for the permuted fits, or LinAlgError for the add_const=True case), the discrete-lattice test fails with an order-dependent statistic, the manual-ordering test fails because use_distance uses the middle observation, and the center test fails because no FutureWarning is emitted. On the fixed revision all rainbow tests pass, with the same -k selection giving a clean run.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare linear_rainbow(res, use_distance=True) on the original data against the same data under np.random.RandomState(seed).permutation(nobs) for several seeds, and check whether add_constant(x) fits raise LinAlgError.

input_output_examples.input: continuous data, 5 permutations of rows, use_distance=True

risks: The discrete-lattice failure depends on how numpy's non-stable argsort breaks exact distance ties. That tie-breaking can differ across numpy versions and CPU SIMD sort paths (for example x86 AVX512 versus ARM), so the buggy failure may not appear on every platform; it is not guaranteed on arbitrary hardware.

The constant-column LinAlgError depends on whether the singular covariance is exactly singular in floating point. BLAS and rounding differences may make inv succeed on some builds, so that case may not raise everywhere.
The context does not state a tolerance for assert_allclose; the tests use the default rtol 1e-7, and that value is taken from the test code rather than from the passages.
The fixed tests' GH#9103 reference does not match PR#9903 in the title; treat the PR number as the instance id and the test comments as authoritative for the bug.

No dependency version is documented or era-bounded, so the chosen numpy/pandas/scipy versions are an unbounded choice; a much newer or older numpy could change argsort tie behaviour and the LinAlgError outcome.
The Cython build needs a working C compiler; if the build fails, the buggy revision cannot be tested and the nightly wheel would not contain the buggy code.

oracle.reference_source: statsmodels test assertions comparing permuted fits to the unpermuted reference; R lmtest::raintest and Utts (1982) are cited in the context but not used by the test
oracle.why: The property tested is order invariance of the statistic; the tolerance only needs to separate floating-point noise (~1e-15) from the buggy order-dependent spread (~0.17 or larger).

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision the permuted-data F differs from the reference by far more than 1e-7, so assert_allclose raises AssertionError; the add_const=True case raises LinAlgError before the assertion; the discrete test sees 69 distinct F values with spread 0.17; the center test's pytest.warns raises because no FutureWarning is emitted.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the centroid-based Mahalanobis ordering, pseudo-inverse covariance and lexsort tie-break, the permuted statistics agree to floating-point noise, the constant-column model runs without raising, the manual-ordering comparison matches, and center emits the FutureWarning with an unchanged statistic, so all selected rainbow tests pass.
